answer: Sybil resistance rests on a non-transferable bond escrowed per identity: to add a clone, an attacker must lock a fresh deposit in that clone's vault, since transferable tokens would be copied across one wallet cluster. Like a wharf charging per berth, the protocol charges each identity separately, so cost grows linearly while reward stays fixed and a clone farm cannot out-earn one honest agent. A reference graph also makes established agents stake collateral behind new agents, forfeited on proof of cloning, and a prism folding clones into one origin leaves a clone no chain to wander into.
